title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover hysteresis and load-shedding
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: A production incident on 2026-02-28 exposed a cascading regional failover when the SLO enforcer backoff/hysteresis interaction allowed rapid oscillation between healthy and degraded regions. Root cause: timing/race between queue-threshold-based load-shedding and regional backoff counters that reset too quickly under bursty traffic, causing neighboring regions to simultaneously initiate failover. This PR contains a hotfix to stabilize the SLO enforcer behavior and add defensive guards to prevent thrashing.

What this PR does: - Introduces hysteresis windows on per-region backoff counters so backoff increments and decrements require sustained condition for a configurable period. - Adds a small randomized jitter to backoff decay timers to avoid synchronized decay across regions. - Tightens the ordering and locking around queue threshold checks and the SLO enforcer state transition (reduces race windows). - Backs out the recent aggressive auto-scaling trigger (ENG-2399) by making it opt-in behind a runtime feature flag (slo.enforcer.opt_in_aggressive_autoscale=false by default). - Adds integration and load test scenarios that replicate the incident pattern and assert no multi-region failover within 10 minutes under the same traffic spike. - Adds observability: new metrics slo_enforcer.hysteresis_window_seconds and slo_enforcer.jitter_seconds and a dashboard link.

Why this is safe to merge as a hotfix: - Change is configuration-first (defaults are conservative). - Added feature flag allows quick rollback of the aggressive behavior. - New tests reproduce the incident pattern locally and in CI stress runs. - Small, focused code changes in the SLO enforcer and regional coordinator.

Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests for the hysteresis logic and backoff counter state transitions. - Stress integration tests in perf-canary that replay the previous incident traffic pattern (passes after this change). - Canary rollout to eu-west-1 (3 nodes) for 1 hour with synthetic traffic; no cascading failovers observed. - CI: build, unit, integration, lint, and e2e stress run (all green after a single re-run).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main and feature-flag enabled=false (safe default). 2) Canary to two regions (eu-west-1 then us-west-2) for 2 hours each. 3) Monitor slo_enforcer.* metrics and regional-failover alerts. 4) If stable, enable opt-in aggressive auto-scale only after additional telemetry (ENG-2399 follow-up).

Rollback: Flip slo.enforcer.enable_hysteresis=false or revert the feature flag; postmortem includes a one-click runbook (runbook ID: ENG-2345-RB).

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced incident in perf-canary - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration stress tests added - [x] Metrics & dashboard updated - [x] Feature-flagged changes - [x] Reviewed and approved by SREs

References: Linear ENG-2345, ENG-2399; support ticket SUP-9876.
